FakeVAE. MiniT2I runs in an RGB pixel-space "latent" (in_channels = 3), so there is no learned VAE — the pipeline uses FakeVAE and a plain clamp for decode. Three fork sites in stable-diffusion.cpp must add MiniT2I:

1) FakeVAE construction (fork ~line 1045):
   change  `if (version == VERSION_CHROMA_RADIANCE || version == VERSION_HIDREAM_O1) {`
   to      `if (version == VERSION_CHROMA_RADIANCE || version == VERSION_HIDREAM_O1 || sd_version_is_minit2i(version)) {`

2) get_latent_channel() (fork ~line 3505, inside the sd_version_is_dit branch): add
       `} else if (sd_version_is_minit2i(version)) {`
       `    latent_channel = 3;`

3) decode_first_stage() (fork ~line 3674): the fork currently special-cases only PiD:
       `if (sd_version_is_pid(version)) {`
       `    return sd::ops::clamp((x + 1.f) * 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f);`
   extend the condition to `if (sd_version_is_pid(version) || sd_version_is_minit2i(version)) {`.

No VAE factory dispatch code is needed beyond enabling FakeVAE. Confidence high — upstream is explicit on all three.
